candidate_findings.title: Seglog source-of-truth is missing an executable append and replay contract
candidate_findings.gap: The core declares replayable durable records and seglog authority but does not define the canonical event envelope, event/schema version, sequence allocation, causation, idempotency key, append acknowledgement boundary, transaction grouping, checkpoint/watermark, or replay-conflict behavior.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: After a crash or retry, independent implementations can duplicate effects, reorder dependent events, acknowledge data before it is durable, or rebuild redb projections to different states while each still claims conformance.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Define a versioned EventRecord envelope and append protocol, including project/run partitioning, globally or partition-monotonic ordering, durability acknowledgement, atomic batch boundaries, idempotent producer rules, checkpoint semantics, replay ordering, poison-event handling, and deterministic rebuild acceptance fixtures.

candidate_findings.title: Projection revalidation is not an atomic safety protocol
candidate_findings.gap: The core requires direct canonical revalidation and says storage decides when authority is withheld, but it never defines what counts as sensitive, what version or generation is validated, how long validation remains valid, or how the mutation is atomically conditioned on the validated state.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: A projection can change between revalidation and action. Displaying currentness or actionable flags does not prevent a time-of-check/time-of-use mutation against a superseded generation or changed permission state.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Provide a per-action trust matrix, canonical version/watermark token, freshness rules, disabled-state reasons, revalidation failure behavior, and compare-and-act semantics that bind the mutation to the validated record version, generation, actor, and authority snapshot.

the missing requirement is `trust-state` operationalization, where storage decides when stale or degraded projections can be inspected, when canonical revalidation is required, and when mutation or export authority is withheld.
Any direct record view that allows action must display currentness, generation match, superseded yes/no, and actionable yes/no before surfacing mutation controls

candidate_findings.title: Concern lifecycle ordering contradicts the stated meanings of resolved and dismissed
candidate_findings.gap: The lifecycle is written as a linear `active -> acknowledged -> resolved -> dismissed` chain, yet dismissed is defined as rejecting or hiding actionable framing and resolved as an underlying truth change. The chain therefore requires dismissal after resolution and omits plausible direct transitions such as active-to-dismissed or acknowledged-to-dismissed.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Projectors and GUIs can disagree about whether dismissal closes a still-real concern, whether a resolved concern can be dismissed, which state controls notifications, and how undo or reopening should behave.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Replace the arrow chain with an explicit finite-state transition table defining allowed sources and destinations, guards, actor authority, required rationale/evidence, terminal versus nonterminal states, merge/split/supersession effects, compensating undo, and invalid-transition behavior.

evidence_refs.excerpt: Concern lifecycle remains `active -> acknowledged -> resolved -> dismissed`;

`dismissed` means the presentation was intentionally hidden or `/rejected` as actionable framing and requires rationale when it disagrees with corroborated or `/high-severity` evidence; `resolved` means the underlying truth changed and records `resolution_kind`.

candidate_findings.title: Worktree lifecycle and Source Control posture vocabularies have no deterministic mapping
candidate_findings.gap: Storage declares baseline, active, suspect, restoring, cleanup_eligible, historical, and other lifecycle states distinct, while Source Control uses live, dirty, conflict, orphaned, recovering, and a smaller overlapping set. It then calls the first vocabulary a migration alias for the second without defining one-to-one, one-to-many, or orthogonal dimensions.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: A worktree can be both active and dirty, or historical and archived, so forcing these concepts into one state risks losing information. Cleanup or remove controls may be enabled from an incorrect projection, producing destructive behavior or misleading GUI truth.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Define separate persisted dimensions if appropriate, plus the exact mapping, precedence, legal transitions, coexistence constraints, derived UI posture, cleanup eligibility guards, tombstone/history rules, and migration fixtures for every legacy value.

evidence_refs.excerpt: Lane/worktree lifecycle keeps `baseline`, `active`, `suspect`, `restoring`, `retained`, `cleanup_eligible`, `archived`, `removed`, and `historical` as distinct states.

Source Control uses a concrete worktree-first row posture: `live`, `dirty`, `conflict`, `orphaned`, `recovering`, `retained`, `archived`, and `removed`. The compact lifecycle vocabulary `baseline/active/suspect/restoring/retained/cleanup_eligible/archived/removed/historical` is a migration alias for those individually queryable states, not a collapsed generic worktree state.

candidate_findings.title: Blocked-episode identity and allowed actions are not concurrency-safe
candidate_findings.gap: `blocked_sequence` is the identity component within run/node scope, and allowed action IDs are persisted, but the core does not define atomic sequence allocation, uniqueness across restart, retry idempotency, episode lifecycle, action authorization, expiry, or action-result recording.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Concurrent blockers or replayed events can reuse a sequence, and a stale client can invoke an action that was allowed for an earlier episode. Recovery can then attach to the wrong block or run twice.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Define monotonic sequence allocation and persistence, blocked-episode states and transition events, immutable episode identity, allowed-action versioning and expiry, actor/permission checks, idempotency keys, compare-and-act preconditions, action outcome records, and stale-episode rejection behavior.

evidence_refs.excerpt: `blocked_sequence` is the identity component for `object_kind = blocked_episode` inside `{ run_id, node_id }` scope; canonical projectors preserve it when writing blocked projections, recovery refs, and Ledger routes.
`allowed_action_ids` and `allowed_action_ids[]` identify permitted direct actions;

candidate_findings.title: Compatibility ingestion has no versioned transformation or rejection policy
candidate_findings.gap: Storage may ingest a large family of legacy tier and event names and promises subordinate searchable aliases, but the core does not define per-alias transformations, source-version detection, field precedence, conflict handling, cutover, deduplication, unknown-event quarantine, or migration completion evidence.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Two producers can encode the same execution under legacy and canonical identities, causing duplicate attempts, split histories, or tier authority to leak back into runtime state. Silent best-effort conversion makes data loss and semantic drift hard to detect.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Provide a versioned migration matrix for every accepted alias, deterministic canonical output, conflict and unknown-input behavior, idempotent upgrade checkpoints, producer deprecation/cutover rules, lineage preservation, dead-letter observability, and golden before/after fixtures.

Lane/worktree lifecycle keeps `baseline`, `active`, `suspect`, `restoring`, `retained`, `cleanup_eligible`, `archived`, `removed`, and `historical` as distinct states.

Source Control uses a concrete worktree-first row posture: `live`, `dirty`, `conflict`, `orphaned`, `recovering`, `retained`, `archived`, and `removed`. The compact lifecycle vocabulary `baseline/active/suspect/restoring/retained/cleanup_eligible/archived/removed/historical` is a migration alias for those individually queryable states, not a collapsed generic worktree state.

`blocked_sequence` is the identity component for `object_kind = blocked_episode` inside `{ run_id, node_id }` scope; canonical projectors preserve it when writing blocked projections, recovery refs, and Ledger routes.
`allowed_action_ids` and `allowed_action_ids[]` identify permitted direct actions;

Storage may ingest `run.tier_started`, `run.tier_completed`, `run.persona_stage_changed`, `tier_runtime_record`, `tier_id`, `tier_type`, `tier-era`, `tier-start`, `tier-boundary`, `PuppetMasterEvent`, `PuppetMasterEvent::*`
Migration aliases stay explicit but subordinate.
That template carries the shared envelope, lineage refs, status, actor identity, timing, evidence refs, artifact refs, source refs, and `/contracts` linkage

`project_summary.v1` rolls up current active run state, dominant concern/blocked owner (`/blocked`), highest-severity attention state, current pressure summary, and health/config integrity (`/config`) without replacing project attention records.
Project `/card` and badge rollups show the highest-severity active item plus a count, while the attention center keeps each active item separately object-linked;
Startup recovery, counter ceilings/backoff (`/backoff`), DAE `/jail` lifecycle, and attention `/blocked` escalation keep authoritative owner refs in storage records.
status values are `active | cooled_down | resolved | invalidated`, with `cooled_down` preserved as a queryable state rather than flattened into resolved.

Large-run density is a real-world storage concern: many active and historical concerns, corroboration `/review/promotion/recovery` records, retained lanes, and cleanup-eligible lanes/worktrees (`/worktrees`) must remain separately queryable instead of collapsing into one graph-only summary.
# Storage plan (seglog, redb, Tantivy, projectors)

Recovery records include `recovery kind`, `safe-point restore`, `restart reconciliation`, `blocked prerequisite resolution`, `lane/worktree restore`, `target scope refs`, `trigger reason`, `preconditions`, `result`, `resulting attempt/run linkage`, and `affected concern refs`.

`destination_surface`, `destination_tab`, `object_kind`, `object_id`, `record_id`, `artifact_id`, `attempt_id`, `lane_id`, `worktree_id`, `usage_event_ref`, `filter_payload`, `inspector_target`, `scroll_target`, and `focus_behavior` are canonical command routing fields.
Usage/artifact flows must not keep `usage_event_ref` as a first-class top-level route selector; storage normalizes it into object identity and receipt/usage joins.

Role-scoped execution uses `execution_role` plus `actor_role`, `allowed_roles?`, and `disallowed_roles?`; effective-resolution/runtime and usage records identify which role actually executed the attempt/message.

Record-family split stays explicit: review finding is produced by a review/corroboration/validation flow, concern is a durable tracked issue/observation (`/observation`), blocked episode is a runtime execution stop with canonical recovery metadata, and annotation is a document-review instruction/comment object.
Runtime records for side-effectful or externally-scoped actions include an `operational-identity` block distinct from provider account identity.

Records and artifacts stay separate: a record is the canonical structured object in Ledger/export/search/routing (`/export/search/routing`), while an artifact is the file/blob/renderable (`/blob/renderable`) output linked from that record.

Active-agent runtime truth, file-activity claims, operation state, crash/abort/unregister state, and coordination snapshots are owned by the `coordination.*` EventRecord families and `coordination_*_projection.v1` redb projections, not by `project_state` or `active-agents.json`.

`WorktreeGitImprovement.md` owns operational behavior, cleanup/archive/remove rules including `/archive/remove`, and UI expectations for Source Control and Orchestrator; storage owns persisted lifecycle/history state and projection joins.
`/account/execution-role` and provider/account/execution-role precedence are resolved by the shared account/runtime contracts
route identity itself belongs to the shared command/open contract.
`/verification/routing` coverage is required for runtime-era actions and records before `/matrix/gate` decisions can claim complete authority.
